contribution.position: I hold my earlier reliability position, and I must correct the qa role's reading of the evidence: qa claims artifact:perf-report shows p99_latency of 180ms within the 250ms budget, but the artifact as listed actually reports p99_latency of 410ms at peak load against that same 250ms budget — a 64% overrun, not a comfortable margin. The 180ms figure does not appear anywhere in the artifact list, so qa's 'risk is contained' conclusion rests on a datum that does not exist in this debate's evidence. This strengthens rather than weakens the reliability concern I raised: the only latency measurement on record shows the budget breached at peak, and artifact:incident-log documents two sev2 retry-storm incidents last quarter, the exact failure mode that excess latency under load feeds. Product's cost evidence (artifact:cost-sheet) and ops's runbook (artifact:ops-runbook) are unchallenged but do not bear on runtime reliability. The green functional suite (artifact:test-report) still says nothing about behavior under load. Nothing new has appeared since my last turn to mitigate the measured latency regression or the retry-storm history, so on the reliability axis the evidence on record continues to point against shipping in the current state until the 410ms peak-load p99 is explained or reduced.
